text.p: Here is how major stock markets outside the United States ended on Friday.

LONDON - UK shares finished a disappointing week in a more upbeat mood as Wall Street finally looked like breaking a string of recent losses on Friday. The re-emergence of bid speculation in the electricity industry also played a part and after an uncertain start which saw the FTSE 100 drop further below the 4,000 mark, UK shares finished 23 points higher at 4,022.4 a fall of 30.7 on the week.

FRANKFURT- Shares closed bourse trade weaker, but off the session's lows after comments by Bundesbank council members suggested further interest rate cuts could not be ruled out. The DAX index of 30 leading stocks closed floor dealings down 4.21 points at 2,674.22, down 59.98 from last Friday. In post-bourse trade the index stood at 2,690.79 up 8.85.

PARIS - French stocks finished higher on Friday, propelled by a rise in bond prices on expectations of European interest rate cuts, but the bourse retreated from its best levels on Wall Street's weak performance in early trade. The blue-chip CAC-40 index closed up 10.81 points or 0.5 percent at 2,162.43 a fall of 22.8 since last week.

ZURICH - Swiss shares shook off early weakness to close near the day's highs, profiting from gains in some blue chip shares. "I am very surprised the market held so well, it did not look that way in the beginning", a dealer said, citing Thursday's losses on Wall Street. The broad SPI closed up 0.16 percent, or 3.78 points, to 2,413.20 a drop of 25.39 from a week ago.

TOKYO - The Nikkei average fell for the fifth successive day as investor sentiment was bogged down by uncertainties over a new coalition government as well as the state of the economy. The Nikkei shed 263.52 points or 1.25 percent to end at 20,739.97, falling 872.33 from last week.

HONG KONG - Stocks closed lower due to pre-weekend profit-taking and caution regarding the near-term outlook for the local market induced by Wall Street's weakness. The Hang Seng Index closed 85.18 points down at 12,388.38, a loss of 121.67 from last Friday. Turnover remained robust at HK$6.65 billion, down slightly from Thursday's HK$7.12 billion.

SYDNEY - Shares closed sharply lower as profit-taking erased all of Thursday's record-breaking gains following another fall on Wall Street. Options exercises, following Thursday's October series expiries, drove volumes and the vast majority of turnover put through the market was before the start of trade. The All Ordinaries index ended 42.4 points lower at 2,335.2, down 19.8 from seven days ago.

JOHANNESBURG - Battling to shrug off earlier comments by Reserve Bank Governor Chris Stals, South African shares were knocked by nerves as the rand slid to a new low against the dollar. Suffering from softness for much of the week, shares lost ground soon after the rand hit a new all-time low against the dollar. It was last bid at 4.6110 against the U.S. currency. Overall index off 31.2 points to 6,985.2 down 18.6 on the week, industrials lose 15.1 points to 8,258.9 up 0.5 from last Friday and golds off 9.9 points to 1,703.8. This was up 35.4 from a week ago.
